keys.AI.ai_answer_questions: Answer a couple of quick questions so the description is accurate:
keys.AI.ai_desc_add_hint: AI places your addition where you ask, keeps everything else, and shows the full result to review before applying.
keys.AI.ai_desc_add_placeholder: What should I add — and where? (e.g. add acceptance criteria, or a note under What to do)
keys.AI.ai_desc_intent_hint: Leave blank to generate from the title.
keys.AI.ai_failed: Couldn't generate a description. Please try again.
keys.AI.ai_proposal_id_hint: The won proposal this project came from. Used to tie the project back to the bid it originated from.
keys.AI.ai_skills_hint: Skills this project needs. The AI also suggests skills from your description — you can adjust them on the review step.
keys.Accounts.always_1: Every timer an agent starts is logged against you and stamped as agent time, not your own hours.
keys.Accounts.always_1_where: Modules/Agents/actions.js — timelog.start writes actorType, viaAccount and runId
keys.Accounts.always_2: Every allowed call and every refusal is written to the audit log with the account type and the token behind it.
keys.Accounts.always_3: A token scoped to projects can only see tasks in those projects.
keys.Accounts.always_3_where: Modules/Mcp/tools.js — scopeFilter restricts every tool to the token's projectIds
keys.Accounts.attrib_empty: No agent has run here yet. Start one from the agents list and it will appear with its account type.
keys.Accounts.attrib_lead: Person, tool, then account type — in that order, everywhere.
keys.Accounts.attrib_title: How it reads on the task
keys.Accounts.billing_q_body: when a client asks what the agent hours were, you can show the tasks, the links and who supervised them, and whether the run was billed to the workspace at all.
keys.Accounts.boundary_source: These are not promises added to a page. The left column is what the audit, run and timesheet rows actually store; the right column is what the code has no field for.
keys.Accounts.by_source_source: Elapsed time on agent runs recorded in this workspace, split by the account each run went through. Human hours are counted separately on the timesheet.
keys.Accounts.cli_comment_add: add AlianHub as an MCP server (any CLI agent)
keys.Accounts.cli_others_note: Other tools: give them the same URL and Authorization header — check your tool's docs for its exact command.
keys.Accounts.cli_url_guess: The token appears here once you mint one, and the server returns the exact URL with it.
keys.Accounts.cli_url_minted: This is the exact URL and token the server just returned. The token is not shown again.
keys.Accounts.expiry_list_empty: Every active token in this workspace has an expiry.
keys.Accounts.expiry_list_lead: Every active token in this workspace that has no expiry, with the day it stops working. Only the owner of a token can replace it: ask them to create a new token with an expiry, then revoke this one.
keys.Accounts.expiry_list_over_max_lead: Tokens made to last longer than the maximum of {n} days stop working {n} days after the maximum took effect. Their owners should create a new token with a shorter expiry, then revoke the old one.
keys.Accounts.expiry_list_title: Tokens that still need an expiry
keys.Accounts.expiry_list_unchecked: no expiry · grace cannot be checked right now
keys.Accounts.field_email_hint: The address on your own provider account
keys.Accounts.lifetime_capped_until: exceeds the maximum lifetime · works until {d}
keys.Accounts.lifetime_stopped_on: exceeds the maximum lifetime · stopped on {d}
keys.Accounts.lifetime_unchecked: exceeds the maximum lifetime · cannot be checked right now
keys.Accounts.link_form_lead: Pick how your agent work should run. This records the mode and provider against your user; it never asks for, stores or proxies a key.
keys.Accounts.link_lead: Use your own Claude Code, Antigravity, Cursor or Codex account for work in AlianHub, then paste one command into your CLI.
keys.Accounts.mode_local_sub: Ollama or vLLM on your GPU, no external account
keys.Accounts.mode_personal_sub: Their own Claude Code. AlianHub never holds a key
keys.Accounts.mode_workspace_sub: One API key in settings, shared by everyone
keys.Accounts.modes_lead: Three ways an agent can run in this workspace. A workspace can allow more than one, and every screen shows which one did the work.
keys.Accounts.never_body: These are not permissions that have been switched off. They are not in the action list at all, so a compromised token has nothing to switch on, and an attempt is refused with an audit id.
keys.Accounts.never_title: Absent from the registry, in every mode
keys.Accounts.no_modes_allowed: No mode is currently permitted for linking. Ask an owner or admin to change the policy.
keys.Accounts.no_tokens: No tokens yet. Mint one to connect a CLI agent.
keys.Accounts.policy_local_effect: Runs against a model inside your own network.
keys.Accounts.policy_need_one: At least one mode has to stay allowed.
keys.Accounts.policy_personal_effect: Members may link their own CLI account and mint a scoped token.
keys.Accounts.policy_read_only: READ ONLY, AN OWNER OR ADMIN SETS THIS
keys.Accounts.policy_refusal_note: A mode that is off is refused with the reason shown, not hidden: linking an account and minting a token both check this policy before anything is written.
keys.Accounts.policy_workspace_effect: Server-side runs on the workspace key, including scheduled agents.
keys.Accounts.recommended_body: workspace key for the scheduled agents, because they are cheap and predictable; personal accounts for hands-on CLI coding work; and the self-hosted option available so a customer who refuses external models still gets the whole product. All three can run at once.
keys.Accounts.row_best_local: Regulated teams, air-gapped installs, or anyone who will not send work data out.
keys.Accounts.row_best_personal: Hands-on coding work: your developers, on their own terms.
keys.Accounts.row_best_workspace: Scheduled agents: daily PM, reporter, smart assign.
keys.Accounts.row_can_local: Everything in the allow-list, but slower and weaker on hard reasoning.
keys.Accounts.row_can_personal: Only what that person can do, only while they are at the keyboard. No scheduled runs.
keys.Accounts.row_can_workspace: Everything in the allow-list, including unattended and scheduled runs.
keys.Accounts.row_offboarding_personal: Revoke their AlianHub token and the link dies. Their subscription and history stay theirs.
keys.Accounts.row_offboarding_workspace: Nothing to do. The key is the company's.
keys.Accounts.row_pays_local: Nobody, per run. Electricity and one GPU.
keys.Accounts.row_pays_personal: The developer's own subscription. Workspace spend for this work is $0.
keys.Accounts.row_pays_workspace: The company. One bill, predictable, capped per agent.
keys.Accounts.row_where_personal: On the developer's machine. AlianHub only receives the result of the work: comments, status, PR link, hours.
keys.Accounts.row_where_workspace: Server-side, from AlianHub. Needed for scheduled agents that run with nobody logged in.
keys.Accounts.rule_allow_list_body: A personal account gets exactly the tools listed on the setup panel. The registry decision takes no account mode as an argument, so paying for your own model does not buy extra permissions.
keys.Accounts.rule_allow_list_where: Modules/Agents/registry.js — evaluate takes an action key and its params, never a mode
keys.Accounts.rule_caps: A cap pauses the agent, it does not fail quietly.
keys.Accounts.rule_caps_body: When workspace-billed spend reaches an agent's monthly cap the agent is paused with the reason recorded, and the next run is refused with that same reason.
keys.Accounts.rule_caps_where: Modules/Agents/runs.js — recordSpend pauses at the cap and canStart refuses once it is reached
keys.Accounts.rule_contractor: A contractor wants their own account.
keys.Accounts.rule_contractor_body: Allowed, but their token can be scoped to the projects they are in. Then even the next-task and search tools only return tasks from those projects.
keys.Accounts.rule_contractor_where: Modules/Mcp/tools.js — scopeFilter adds the token's projectIds to every tool query
keys.Accounts.rule_lapses_body: A personal-mode CLI fails on their machine, and AlianHub never sees it: a CLI session creates no run record, so the task simply stays assigned to them with no new activity. Workspace-mode runs do record a failed status with the reason.
keys.Accounts.rule_lapses_where: Modules/Agents/runs.js — a failed status is written by the server-side run engine only
keys.Accounts.rule_leaves_body: Unlinking clears their account and deactivates every agent token they hold in this workspace. Their comments, PRs and logged hours stay on the tasks, attributed to them. Nothing is deleted.
keys.Accounts.rule_leaves_where: Modules/Agents/accounts.js — unlink sets active false on their agent tokens and unsets agentAccount
keys.Accounts.rule_local_spend: Local runs cost the workspace nothing.
keys.Accounts.rule_local_spend_body: Self-hosted runs are treated the same way as personal ones for billing: no workspace dollars, and no contribution to a cap.
keys.Accounts.rule_local_spend_where: Modules/Agents/runs.js — recordSpend excludes both personal and local from billing
keys.Accounts.rule_personal_spend: Personal spend is never the workspace's.
keys.Accounts.rule_personal_spend_body: A run through a personal account records the workspace cost as $0, keeps the estimate separately, and returns before touching the agent's monthly total.
keys.Accounts.rule_personal_spend_where: Modules/Agents/runs.js — recordSpend marks the run as not billed to the workspace
keys.Accounts.rule_reimbursement: Reimbursement is a report, not a feature.
keys.Accounts.rule_reimbursement_body: AlianHub counts tasks and hours through each person's account from its own rows. It never reads a provider invoice, and has no field to store one.
keys.Accounts.rule_reimbursement_where: Modules/Agents/accounts.js — monthlySummary reads timesheet, run and task-link rows only
keys.Accounts.rule_require_mode: An admin can require a mode.
keys.Accounts.rule_require_mode_body: A regulated customer allows local only, and linking or minting anything else is refused with the reason shown rather than the option quietly disappearing.
keys.Accounts.rule_require_mode_where: Modules/Agents/accounts.js link and Modules/ApiTokens/controller.js createMcpToken both check the policy first
keys.Accounts.rule_revoke: Revoking stops future runs and keeps the history.
keys.Accounts.rule_revoke_body: Revoke here deactivates the token, so it stops authenticating immediately. Every audit row, comment and time log it already wrote stays exactly where it is.
keys.Accounts.rule_revoke_where: Modules/ApiTokens/controller.js — verifyToken only accepts an active token; audit rows live in their own collection
keys.Accounts.rule_two_people_body: Both can run agents on it. Each comment is stamped with the actor type, the agent and the account it came through, so a duplicate PR is obvious rather than mysterious.
keys.Accounts.rule_two_people_where: Modules/Agents/actions.js — task.comment stamps actorType, agentId and viaAccount on the comment
keys.Accounts.rule_unattended_body: A scheduled run through a personal account is refused, because nobody should be billed for a run they did not trigger while their laptop was shut.
keys.Accounts.rule_unattended_where: Modules/Agents/runs.js — canStart refuses a scheduled trigger when the account is personal
keys.Accounts.rules_lead: The awkward cases, decided in code rather than left to a conversation. Each rule names where it is enforced.
keys.Accounts.scope_all: Every project you can already open
keys.Accounts.scope_hint: A token scoped to one project cannot reach tasks outside it, whatever the CLI asks for.
keys.Accounts.sees_1: That a run happened, and which task it was on
keys.Accounts.sees_2: Elapsed time, and the hours written to your timesheet
keys.Accounts.sees_3: Every action taken through the allow-list, as an audit row
keys.Accounts.sees_4: The comments, subtasks, status moves and PR links your agent created
keys.Accounts.sees_5: Which account type produced each of them
keys.Accounts.self_hosted_note: Self-hosted means the MCP endpoint is on your network. Your code and your task data never leave it — only the model call does, and that can point at your own GPU.
keys.Accounts.stays_1: Your API key or subscription. AlianHub never receives one.
keys.Accounts.stays_2: Your prompts and chat history. Only the result reaches the server.
keys.Accounts.stays_3: Anything outside the projects your token is scoped to.
keys.Accounts.stays_4: Your provider spend and invoice. Nothing here reads them.
keys.Accounts.step_scoped_current_expires: current credential expires {d}, renewed while the step keeps running
keys.Accounts.step_scoped_empty: No step is running under a credential right now.
keys.Accounts.step_scoped_lead: Credentials the workflow engine minted for steps that are running right now. Each one is tied to one step of one run, is replaced by a fresh one each time the engine extends the step's lease, and stops working when that step settles or its lease runs out. The credential itself is never shown or stored; owners and admins see every run, everyone else the runs they started.
keys.Accounts.strict_note: Every new token needs an expiry and at least one scope. A token without an expiry keeps working for {n} days from when this rule was turned on, or from when the token was made if that is later. Replace it before then.
keys.Accounts.summary_note: Counted from your own timesheet rows, runs and task links inside AlianHub. Your own spend sits on your provider account and nothing here reads it.
keys.Accounts.title: Coding accounts
keys.Accounts.token_expiry_over_max: A token can last at most {n} days. Choose a shorter expiry.
keys.Accounts.token_expiry_required: Choose when the token expires. Tokens without an expiry are no longer issued.
keys.Accounts.token_inherits: A token inherits your permissions and then narrows them. It can never exceed what you can do, and delete, billing and member management are not in the registry at all.
keys.Accounts.token_name_required: Give the token a name so you can recognise it later.
keys.Accounts.token_once: Copy this now. It is not shown again — only its hash is stored.
keys.Accounts.token_scope_read_effect: See the projects, tasks and pages you can already open.
keys.Accounts.token_scope_write_effect: Make the changes your own role allows.
keys.Accounts.undecided_1_body: The numbers above are computed on request and there is no export endpoint, so a reimbursement claim is currently a manual read rather than a file.
keys.Accounts.undecided_2: Per-person visibility of the full call list.
keys.Accounts.undecided_2_body: Every call is audited, but who may read those rows is governed by the existing audit permissions. There is no per-member setting to share or hide the detail.
keys.Accounts.unlink_body: stops all agent work through your account and deactivates every agent token you hold here. Past comments, PRs and hours stay on their tasks; nothing is deleted.
keys.Accounts.why_shape_body: The alternative — the company buys keys for everyone and proxies every call — puts AlianHub in the middle of every prompt a developer writes. That is a privacy problem, a cost problem and a support problem, and developers work around it by using their own CLI outside the tool anyway. Let them keep their own account and their own habits; AlianHub's job is to hand over a good brief and to record what came back.
keys.Accounts.why_split_body: velocity that quietly includes agent hours is a lie you will plan next quarter on. Keep the split visible and your estimates stay usable.
keys.AgentClients.action_failed: That did not work. Try again.
keys.AgentClients.empty: No agent has asked to connect yet.
keys.AgentClients.lead: Outside agents sign in with OAuth. Nobody in this workspace can connect one until an owner or admin approves it here, for the permissions you choose.
keys.AgentClients.load_failed: Agent clients could not be loaded.
keys.AgentClients.off: Outside agent sign-in is off on this server.
keys.AgentClients.private_label: May be delegated tasks in private sprints
keys.AgentClients.revoke_confirm: Revoke {name}? Everyone's connection to it in this workspace ends now.
keys.Ai.actions_lead: Pick what it may do. You can widen this later — start narrow.
keys.Ai.available_actions_note: Every action a skill may emit, and what the guard does with it.
keys.Ai.cap_hint: The agent pauses itself at the cap.
keys.Ai.cli_lead: Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Antigravity work against AlianHub over MCP with a scoped personal token.
keys.Ai.decline_reason_lead: Optional. The agents learn from it, and three declines for the same reason become a suggestion in My Settings.
keys.Ai.decline_reason_placeholder: Or say it in your own words
keys.Ai.delete_blocked_running: Stop its {n} open run(s) before deleting this agent.
keys.Ai.delete_body: Removes the agent and its settings. Past runs, proposals and audit rows stay.
keys.Ai.empty_body: Start from a template. Every agent begins at L0 and earns autonomy.
keys.Ai.empty_declined_body: Declined proposals show here. A decline is a normal outcome, not an error.
keys.Ai.empty_done_body: Approved proposals show here once a person accepts one.
keys.Ai.find_task_hint: Type a task key or a few words of its title
keys.Ai.gate_locked: Only an Owner or Admin can decide this one.
keys.Ai.gate_note: This one needs an Owner or Admin. Production is never offered.
keys.Ai.hub_lead: Each agent is a set of skills, an allowed-action list and an autonomy level. Only the model is external — your data stays on your server.
keys.Ai.job_desc_hint: e.g. Post a standup every weekday and nudge stale tasks.
keys.Ai.l2_preview_lead: Read off this agent's allowed actions and each action's risk rating. Reads always run. A write runs on its own only when this agent is scoped to the project and the change can be undone, stays inside one task and moves no money; everything else goes to the AI Inbox first.
keys.Ai.ladder_rule: Money, production and deletes are always a human.
keys.Ai.low_risk_note: Low risk = comment, nudge, status within a sprint, reports. Sprint moves and assignments still go to the AI Inbox.
keys.Ai.model_pin_empty: No priced model is available on this instance yet, so this agent follows the workspace routing policy.
keys.Ai.model_pin_hint: Every run of this agent uses the pinned model. Only models with a price on file can be pinned.
keys.Ai.never_note: These are not switches — they are absent from the action registry, so a compromised token cannot reach them.
keys.Ai.no_actions_body: The server returned an empty action registry, so no agent can do anything yet.
keys.Ai.no_open_tasks: No open task in this agent's projects.
keys.Ai.no_runs: This agent has not run yet.
keys.Ai.no_skills_body: A skill says what an agent reads, what it asks the model, and what it may change. Write one and assign it to an agent — no deploy.
keys.Ai.nothing_changed: Nothing changed, so nothing was saved.
keys.Ai.pick_one: Pick a proposal to see what it would change.
keys.Ai.queue_clear_body: {approved} approved, {declined} declined. Nothing is waiting on you.
keys.Ai.replay_fetch_truncated: Only the first 32 KB of the body is kept; the hash covers all of it.
keys.Ai.replay_none: No model calls were recorded for this run.
keys.Ai.replay_passages_empty: No passages were retrieved for this call.
keys.Ai.replay_policy: Prompts and responses are redacted per the replay policy: email addresses, tokens and secrets are masked.
keys.Ai.req_brief: a brief of at least 40 characters in the description (intake)
keys.Ai.req_linked_doc: a document linked to the task
keys.Ai.req_pr_link: a pull-request or branch link on the task (review)
keys.Ai.req_project_task: any task in the project it should report on (digest)
keys.Ai.req_public_url: a public URL in the task title or description (QA review)
keys.Ai.revision_rollback: Roll back to #{n} — creates #{next} as a copy and makes it live
keys.Ai.revision_rolled_back: Rolled back to revision {n} as revision {live}.
keys.Ai.revisions_lead: Every save is a numbered revision. A run pins the revision that was live when it started, so it can always name the configuration that produced it.
keys.Ai.revisions_load_failed: Could not load the revision history.
keys.Ai.run_needs_task: Every run works on one task. Pick the task this agent should look at.
keys.Ai.runs_manual_note: Runs start from a task, a mention or an assignment. Scheduling is not available yet.
keys.Ai.scope_lead: Pick the projects this agent may change. With none picked it still reads, but every write is refused.
keys.Ai.settings_read_only: Read only. An owner or admin changes this agent's settings.
keys.Ai.skill_dry_run_lead: What {task} would give this skill, and what it would ask. Nothing is written and no model is called.
keys.Ai.skill_dry_run_note: A dry run reads and renders only. The run itself still needs an agent, its allowed actions and your approval.
keys.Ai.skill_editor_lead: A skill is written in a closed vocabulary: the inputs it needs, what it reads, what it asks, and the actions it may emit. Nothing here runs as code.
keys.Ai.skill_emits_hint: Each mapping turns part of the answer into one change. The agent's allowed actions still cut this down.
keys.Ai.skill_fallback: What to post when the model says nothing
keys.Ai.skill_fallback_hint: Rendered from the gathered data alone, so a run still says what the board already knows. It cannot read the answer.
keys.Ai.skill_gather_hint: Each reader is a call the engine already makes; the template reads its answer as {'{{'}gather.name.field{'}}'}.
keys.Ai.skill_grounded: Hold the answer to the data
keys.Ai.skill_grounded_allow_hours: Hour windows the skill itself names, e.g. 24, 48
keys.Ai.skill_grounded_fields: Answer fields to check, comma separated
keys.Ai.skill_grounded_hint: Drops any sentence or item naming a task or a count the skill did not gather. Leave the first two empty to check nothing.
keys.Ai.skill_grounded_must_name_key: Answer lists that must name a gathered task
keys.Ai.skill_inputs_hint: A run skips when the task lacks one of these, with the reason on the run.
keys.Ai.skill_model_hint: Pin a model for this skill only. A model with no price, or one whose provider is not configured, is refused here rather than at run time.
keys.Ai.skill_read_ask_owner: An instance owner adds hosts to the allowlist under Instance > Egress.
keys.Ai.skill_read_chip_not_declarable: Not allowed as a declared host
keys.Ai.skill_read_credential_empty: No read credential names {host}. An owner or admin adds one under Settings > Integrations > Secrets.
keys.Ai.skill_read_credential_hint: A workspace read credential that names this host. Only its name and handle are shown here, never its value.
keys.Ai.skill_read_err_allowlist_unreadable: The workspace egress allowlist could not be read, so the declared reads were not checked. Try again.
keys.Ai.skill_read_err_credential_host_not_bo: That credential may not be sent to this host. An owner or admin adds the host to it under Settings > Integrations > Secrets.
keys.Ai.skill_read_err_credential_invalid: Choose a credential from the list; a secret value cannot be written here.
keys.Ai.skill_read_err_credential_not_found: That credential is not in this workspace.
keys.Ai.skill_read_err_credential_revoked: That credential is revoked; choose a live one.
keys.Ai.skill_read_err_credential_store_off: The secrets store is off, so no credential can be chosen.
keys.Ai.skill_read_err_credential_store_unava: The secrets store could not be read, so the credential was not checked. Try again.
keys.Ai.skill_read_err_credential_wrong_kind: That secret is not a read credential.
keys.Ai.skill_read_err_host_not_allowed: "{host}" is not on this workspace's egress allowlist. An instance owner adds it under Instance > Egress.
keys.Ai.skill_read_err_invalid_path: The path must start with a single "/" and hold no empty, "." or ".." segments, backslashes, spaces, control characters or "#".
keys.Ai.skill_read_err_link_invalid: This read cannot take that link; choose one from the list.
keys.Ai.skill_read_err_link_undeclared: The skill does not ask the task for "{input}". Tick it under "What the task must carry", or choose another link.
keys.Ai.skill_read_err_path_or_link: Give a path, or choose a link to read.
keys.Ai.skill_read_err_range: Must be a number from {min} to {max}.
keys.Ai.skill_read_err_secret_in_body: This looks like a secret. Keep it in a workspace secret and choose it as a read's credential.
keys.Ai.skill_read_host_address: "{host}" is an address; declare a host name.
keys.Ai.skill_read_host_hint: One exact host name, with a port when it is not 443. No scheme, path or wildcard.
keys.Ai.skill_read_host_path: Declare the host alone; the path goes in its own field.
keys.Ai.skill_read_host_private: "{host}" is a private, local or internal host.
keys.Ai.skill_read_host_scheme: Declare the host alone, without a scheme such as https://.
keys.Ai.skill_read_host_wildcard: Declare one exact host, not a wildcard.
keys.Ai.skill_read_host_wildcard_dns: "{host}" is under a wildcard-DNS service that answers with any address written into the name.
keys.Ai.skill_read_hosts_hint: Up to {max} more exact hosts this read may reach: where a redirect goes, or another host the task's link may point at. Each one is checked against the egress allowlist like the host above.
keys.Ai.skill_read_lead: This reader fetches from one host outside the workspace. The host must be on this workspace's egress allowlist, and it is checked again on every run.
keys.Ai.skill_read_link_hint: Reads the whole URL the task carries, in place of a path. The link must point at the host above or one of the other hosts; a link to any other host skips the run.
keys.Ai.skill_read_link_none: None: build the URL from the host and path
keys.Ai.skill_read_link_none_declared: To read a link from the task, tick one of these under "What the task must carry": {inputs}.
keys.Ai.skill_read_path_hint: Starts with a single "/". Each placeholder is filled from the task or a declared input and sent encoded as one value. Available: {placeholders}
keys.Ai.skill_retire_confirm: Agents and rules keep the key; the skill stops resolving and falls back to the built-in one, if there is one.
keys.Ai.skill_risk_hint: The actions it emits make this {risk}. A floor can only raise it.
keys.Ai.skills_effective_note: The chips are what this agent would allow the skill to do: the skill's actions cut to the agent's allowed actions.
keys.Ai.skills_lead: A skill is a playbook plus the short list of actions it may take. Nothing outside this list can ever run.
keys.Ai.skills_library_lead: Every action an agent can take in this workspace, and the ones it never can.

keys.Ai.soon_home: This becomes the way into AI: one place to ask a question, start an agent and pick up a run that is waiting on you. It is being built now — nothing on this screen is wired yet.
keys.Ai.start_low: Start at L0 or L1. Autonomy is earned by trust, not by a release date.

keys.Ai.trace_copy_failed: The trace id could not be copied.
